caption:
Back in five minutes, said the card on the counter. It was eleven weeks. New stock came in.

This season the feed is a building, and one window lights up with every post.
Shop 1 opens first: the Baguette Tennis Bracelet in ruby-red cubic zirconia, each baguette held at its corners by gold tone claws. About 17 cm. ₹1,599.

Take 2 pieces for 10% off or 3 for 20% off. The bag applies BUY2 or BUY3 for you.

[ baguette tennis bracelet · 18k gold tone plated · shutter's up ]
first_comment: Next door, Shop 2 opens Wednesday evening. Every piece arrives in our blush box · free insured shipping · COD available #NairaFlore #EditionTwo #TennisBracelet #DemiFineJewellery #NairaPetite
alt_text: Short video. An illustrated blush pink Art Deco building at dusk, four storeys of shut windows with a paper lantern beside each, fills the screen. One lantern lights, at the shop on the ground floor, and the view moves in to it: a sage green board carrying the Naira wordmark over a closed green rolling shutter. The shutter rolls up. Inside the shop is dark, and a bracelet shows only as its own white outline on a velvet tray, in front of a small standing card that reads BACK IN 5 MINUTES. A tube light flickers on, the room lights up, and the outline becomes the real photograph: a tennis bracelet of ruby-red baguette stones in gold-tone claws, lying on the blush velvet tray. On the step below: 'eleven weeks, actually. new stock came in.' A brass plate reads SHOP 1. The view pulls back to the whole building with one window lit, then a closing card: Shop 1, ground floor. Baguette Tennis Bracelet, Ruby. Ruby-red cubic zirconia, 18k gold tone plated. ₹1,599. nairaflore.com. One window a post. This was the first. Every piece arrives in our blush box, free insured shipping, COD available.
sound: In-app instrumental (Instagram audio library, no vocals, no lyrics): a solo sitar or sarod alaap over a tanpura drone, unhurried, no percussion (search 'sitar ambient', 'raga instrumental calm'), entering at 0.8 s under the ambience and ducked 4 dB under the shutter (3.2-5.4 s). BAKED into reel.mp4 (synthesised, _build/sfx.py, peak -12.3 dBFS): 0.0-1.2 s building ambience (street hum, a far scooter passing left to right, a few evening birds; the bed stays on low and rises again over the last 0.5 s so the loop meets itself); 0.25 s the lift-bell, one soft brass ding (B5, ~1.2 s decay) as SHOP 1's kandil lights; 3.2-5.4 s the rolling shutter, 33 slat clicks timed to the reel's own shutter curve (the hand-lift stutter included) over a low roll, the rattle running to 5.35 s (last click 5.33 s), ending in a clunk at 5.39 s on the frame the bottom slat seats; 5.49 and 5.61 s two tube tinks on the blinks with the choke's faint hum; 6.97 s a small glass ting on the first sparkle's peak; 12.6 s one low chime (E4-B4-E5) as the end card comes in.

(a) The plate is masked 6 native px above the lip edge (past the edge's own darker last rows) and the face carries on to the foot and 150 px past it (the parallax bleed) as a copy of the plate mirrored about a line 4 px further in and stretched K = 1.6, not the ~8 px x 7.5 the fix describes: the first try at K = 7.5 stretched the velvet's grain into visible vertical streaks at 2x, and the face is one flat tone for its whole ~105 native px ((169, 128, 107) +-2 from 8 to 104 px above the edge), so taking its last ~36 px instead of ~8 keeps both the tone and the grain; the seam is invisible at 2x. (b) Right of the wall's silhouette (4 native px in, feathered 3 px since the photo's edge is out of focus) the plate is cut away, so the room's own SVG back wall (#FBF3EC gradient, its side-wall shade) and the tube's bloom carry on down to the velvet. The plate's aiBleed strips clone the masked plate, so the parallax bleed carries the cut too (tools/bleedcheck.cjs p01: 0 px changed outside the opening at rest, the e = .5 find and pull-back frames viewed clean).

GLINT MASK FORM (final review fix 1): the director's luminance mask is stored as the ALPHA of a white PNG (_build/glint-mask.png), not as a grey luminance image. CSS mask-image on an image is an alpha mask (mask-mode match-source) in the kit's .glint, which sets -webkit-mask-image / mask-image from --src and nothing else, so this is the same mask in the form the kit already consumes, with no mask-mode override that the -webkit- path may ignore. Luma is Rec.709 on the file's encoded values, the scale on which the reel's ruby reads .31. The mask is a runtime asset that lives in p01/_build/ as the fix asked: every page that loads p01.js fetches it (no failed request on any of P1's pages); if it were ever missing, a mask image that fails to load is transparent black, so the glint vanishes and never covers the stones again (checked in the reel's Chromium: --src pointed at a missing file, the 7.15 s frame equals glint-off in 0 px).
